chunk_findings.detail: `_wait4_delta` reads `resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN`, which is the lifetime total of every child this process has already waited for, not the child just spawned. CPU and block IO are subtracted from a snapshot, but `rss_mb` is `after.ru_maxrss` with no baseline. After any earlier child peaked (for example a 200MB helper), `ddflow perf run` of `true` still reports about 200MB RSS, so every later sample is stuck at the process high-water mark. On a long-lived MCP server the same counters are process-global: a second request whose child exits between `before` and the probe is added into this run's `cpu_s` and `io_rw` as well.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perf.py:48

chunk_findings.detail: `run_perf_run` only turns `FileNotFoundError` into `O.refused`. `subprocess.run(["/tmp"])` (or any argv whose argv0 is a directory or not executable) raises `PermissionError` / `IsADirectoryError` out of the API. The docstring says a command that could not run is a refused or failed outcome; given `cmd="/tmp"` the caller gets an exception and no sample line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perf.py:83

chunk_findings.detail: `wrap_command` interpolates `cmd` with no shell quoting, so the string it calls the exact next command is not the command that will be measured. Given `cmd="pytest -q"`, it returns `ddflow perf run --cmd pytest -q`. A shell (or a naive split of that envelope string) binds `--cmd` to `pytest` only and treats `-q` as a separate token; `pytest -k 'a b'` or a command containing `;` is split or executed outside the wrapper. The measuring wrapper therefore runs a different argv than the one requested.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/remote.py:77

chunk_findings.detail: `_valid_env_key` only drops strings containing `/`, `\`, `:`, `@`, space, or newline, so a posted sample can still store a hostname or username. `parse_line('{"wall_s":1,"env":"webserver01"}')` returns `env="webserver01"` (and `"alice"` likewise). That value is kept on the sample and round-trips through `one_line()`, which mixes identity into the metric key despite the contract that ingested env keys are machine-class digests only and must not carry host or user identity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/remote.py:155

chunk_findings.detail: `wrap_command("pytest -q")` is locked to the unquoted string `ddflow perf run --cmd pytest -q`. The declared `cmd` Param is a single optional flag, not `remainder`/`nargs`, so that exact string binds `cmd` to `pytest` and leaves `-q` unbound (or rejected). Any command with a space, quote, or shell metacharacter is not the command the agent was told to run; the surface help even shows quotes (`--cmd 'pytest -q'`) that `wrap_command` does not emit.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_remote.py:75

chunk_findings.detail: `run()` starts the child with `stdout=PIPE` and `stderr=PIPE` and then blocks in `os.wait4` without ever reading those pipes. A command whose stdout or stderr exceeds the pipe buffer (typically 64KiB) fills the pipe, blocks in `write`, and the parent blocks in `wait4` — a deadlock. `ddflow perf run` of `python -c 'print("x"*100000)'` never returns a sample; the previous `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` drained the pipes. Use `DEVNULL` if the output is unused, or `communicate()` before treating the child as finished.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perf.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: `os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)` raises `ValueError` when the child dies from a signal (`WIFSIGNALED`). That exception is not an `OSError`, so it escapes `run_perf_run` instead of becoming `O.failed`. Given `cmd` that is `kill -9`'d (or any wrapper target that receives SIGTERM/SIGKILL), the caller gets an uncaught `ValueError` and no sample line. `subprocess.CompletedProcess.returncode` used to be negative for signals and fell through to the non-zero `O.failed` path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perf.py:69
